main_text.p: iii.cap.iii. testatur, Græcos πραγματικὸς[?] Iuris interpretes uocasse. Et li.XII.ca.iii. Neq;« ego sum (inquit) nostri mo« moris ignarus, oblitusue eorum« qui uelut ad arculas sedet, &« tela agentibus subministrat:« neque idem Græcos quoq;« nescio factitasse, unde nomē« his pragmaticorum factum« est. Quod idem Antonius libro de Oratore i. his confirmat uerbis: Itaque Græci,« difertissimi homines, mini-stros habent in causis Iurisperitos, cum ipsi sint imperitissimi: (sic enim legendum arbitror) & qui (ut abste paulo ante distum est) pragma-

page.notes: The line-end breaks "mo« / ris" and "Iurispe« / ritos" and "pau« / lo" and "ar« / bitror" carry no printed hyphen, so the words are written whole. "mini-" and "imperitis-" are hyphenated in print and kept. The Greek word on the first line is hard to read; the letters are approximate and marked [?]. The « marks are printed quotation marks at line ends and are kept as printed. "abste" and "distum" are kept as printed spellings. The left and right edges of the scan show no further text. The running head is given without the page number.
